Yeah, franchises tend to charge you a bit more than you'd expect to use their logo, but that's money and time you don't have to spend making your own brand. You've already got a bit of recognition and 'free' advertising coming from them. In return for you not having to do it, yeah, they charge you. Sometimes exorbitantly, for sure, but it's worth it in the long run if you pick the right franchise for the right area and expand aggressively.

Personally, I'm going to advise you to stay away from cleaners. From what I've been told, they don't have a very big profit margin and tend to go under more easily than others. Generally food services are your best bet for filling a niche. Just look around your area and see what you don't have, then make a list and start investigating to see what company is going to be the best fit for your goals and locale. Doing that, you should end up with at least a half dozen businesses whose models you can pit against each other and find what works best for you.
